pr_title: Match config entries for dlna_dmr based on device MAC, in addition to UDN
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Use the MAC address of DLNA DMR devices to try to match them to existing `dlna_dmr` config entries, and abort config flow if a match is found. Ordinarily a devices UDN (unique device name) is used as the config entry `unique_id`, because the UDN is meant to be unique and stable. However, some devices regenerate their UDN at each boot, causing a new config flow to be started each time. To catch this case, the MAC address is used as an additional identifier.

In the case that two devices have the same MAC address, they can still be added manually.

This change also uses the newly obtained MAC address as a device entry connection, so that embedded DLNA DMRs can be linked to their parent device. For example, DLNA software in a smart TV.

Credit is due to @StevenLooman for the original idea and implementation of MAC matching in the `upnp` integration.

Hey there @stevenlooman, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`dlna_dmr`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L250) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Great work! It is unfortunate devices don't seem to behave according to spec, but fortunately we can work around this.

I'm thinking about adding the host (IP) of the device as an identifiers as well for `upnp` (as was before?), dependent on what the results of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/73844 will be. Though that might only work for routers which usually have a static IP anyway.

> Great work!

Thanks :smile: 

> It is unfortunate devices don't seem to behave according to spec, but fortunately we can work around this.

Misbehaving devices seems to be the majority of bug reports at this point :frowning_face: 

> I'm thinking about adding the host (IP) of the device as an identifiers as well for `upnp` (as was before?), dependent on what the results of #73844 will be. Though that might only work for routers which usually have a static IP anyway.

The `dlna_dmr` integration also uses the location of the root description document as another way to match devices. I went with the full URL so that if two different devices manage to swap IP addresses, they are less likely to be mistaken for each other, since the URL path tends to vary between manufacturers..

> The `dlna_dmr` integration also uses the location of the root description document as another way to match devices. I went with the full URL so that if two different devices manage to swap IP addresses, they are less likely to be mistaken for each other, since the URL path tends to vary between manufacturers..

Smart. But be aware that some devices tend to randomize the port their http server is listening on.

> > The `dlna_dmr` integration also uses the location of the root description document as another way to match devices. >

That's ok. I'd rather a false negative than a false positive for matching, in this case, considering that the MAC address is a stronger identifier.

<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

That does look annoying. Can you please post the root description XML for the device?

If you have debug logging enabled for `homeassistant.components.ssdp` then you should see lines starting with `[homeassistant.components.ssdp] Discovery info: SsdpServiceInfo(`. Within that line will be `'_location_original': '<URL>'`, where `<URL>` will be the URL to download the device's root description XML from.

It'd be even better if you could get this file again, a second time, after turning the TV off and on again (or whatever it is that causes it to pop up yet another discovery).

While you're waiting for a fix, you may be able to disable DLNA within the TV's settings.
Perhaps the device is also choosing a random UDN (Unique Device Name) during start up/regularly. The `upnp` component does handle this, perhaps the same logic can be applied to this component.

review_comments: Is this data not available from the upnp data?

Unfortunately not in a standardised way. Some devices will report it in a manufacturer-specific field of the UPnP device description, but it's so uncommon and and the field name varies so it is effectively useless.
Why should we use this as a secondary identifier. If we're going to get the MAC, why wouldn't we always use it as identifier ?

As you identified below, the MAC address is not reported by the DLNA API, and the [developer docs](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/config_entries_config_flow_handler#unique-id-requirements) state good reasons not to use it as a primary unique ID in this case. 

Unfortunately some devices purport to be DLNA compliant but break from the spec in some ways, and this PR is adding a heuristic to deal with certain cases of breakage.
